meta.task_prompt:
Implement GitHub issue #9 on this repo: "add redis caching in auth proxy for kanban endpoints."

There is already a shared Redis client at `internal/pkg/redis/main.go`, and it is
already used elsewhere in the codebase (see `internal/app/server.go` and
`internal/pkg/server/permissions/perm.go` for the existing usage pattern). Follow
that same pattern rather than inventing a new one.

Scope:
- Add caching for the read paths in `internal/pkg/server/routes/kanban.go`.
- Add cache invalidation on the corresponding write paths, so a write never
  leaves a stale cached read behind.
- Pick sane key naming and TTLs consistent with how the existing Redis usage in
  this repo does it.
- This repo currently has no test files. Do not feel obligated to introduce a
  whole test framework for this change, but do double check the code compiles
  and, if there's an easy way to sanity-check the caching behavior manually
  (e.g. a local run), do that.

When you are done, close with a single clear paragraph summarizing exactly what
you changed and why — that summary becomes the pull request's title and body
verbatim, so make it read like a real PR description, not an internal note.

code_review.summary: The diff adds read-through caching to four kanban GET handlers (getKanban, GetLabel, getItem, exportKanban) and one invalidation call in createKanban, all in internal/pkg/server/routes/kanban.go. It follows the existing GetLabels/getItems shape: GetItemFromRedis, then an X-cache: HIT header, then StructToMap + AddItemToRedis with the helper's 24h TTL. It should not merge as it stands. The getKanban change breaks the endpoint: GET /kanban returns a plain-text board id on a miss, but on a hit it returns `{}` as JSON. The engine's own probe at trace line 89 confirmed this. The task said a write must never leave a stale cached read behind, and that requirement is not met. The comment write handlers never invalidate the getItem or export caches, even though items embed their comments. createLabel only deletes `board:Labels`, so the new `board:Export` entry stays stale. The getItem and GetLabel cache keys are built from the client-supplied X-Board header, so a request without that header (or with a different one) writes an entry that the board-prefix sweep never removes. Nothing in the run compiled the code. The PR title and body also describe a different change: they say only create-path invalidation was done and read caching was not.

findings.summary: getKanban caches a bare string through the map-only GetItemFromRedis/AddItemToRedis helpers, so every cache hit returns `{}` as JSON instead of the board id as plain text.
findings.failure_scenario: database.GetKanban returns a string such as "boardid123". AddItemToRedis stores the JSON `"boardid123"`. On the next GET /kanban, GetItemFromRedis unmarshals that into map[string]interface{}, fails silently, and returns an empty non-nil map. `resCache != nil` is true, so the handler responds `200 {}` with a JSON content type instead of `boardid123` as text/plain. Clients that read the board id from this endpoint get garbage for up to 24h. The engine reproduced this in /tmp/niltest3.go (trace line 89: `false map[]`, `treated as HIT with garbage data`).
findings.suggested_fix: Cache the raw string directly: `redis.Rdb.Get(ctx, key).Result()` on read, and `redis.Rdb.Set(ctx, key, res, 24*time.Hour)` on write. Return it with `c.String` on both hit and miss. Alternatively, wrap it as `map[string]interface{}{"boardId": res}` before caching and unwrap it on a hit, still responding with c.String. Either way, add a string-typed helper to internal/pkg/redis rather than reusing the map helper.

findings.summary: The new getItem cache (and the export cache) is never invalidated by AddComment, UpdateComment or DeleteComment, even though Item embeds its comments.
findings.failure_scenario: GET /kanban/item?id=X caches `board:item:X` for 24h. Then POST /kanban/comment?item_id=X adds a comment. That handler touches no cache key, so every later GET /kanban/item?id=X (and GET /kanban/export) keeps returning the item without the new comment until the TTL expires. The task explicitly requires that a write never leave a stale cached read behind.
findings.suggested_fix: In AddComment, UpdateComment and DeleteComment, call `redis.DeleteAllKeysPrefix(request.Header.Get("X-Board"))` after the RPC succeeds, as createItem/updateItem/DeleteItem already do. UpdateComment and DeleteComment only have a comment_id. If X-Board is not reliably sent there, either require item_id/board on those routes, or leave getItem uncached.

findings.summary: The new `boardId:Export` cache goes stale after a label is created, because createLabel only deletes `board:Labels`, not the whole board prefix.
findings.failure_scenario: GET /kanban/export caches the full board export. POST /kanban/label then adds a label and deletes only `<board>:Labels`. The next GET /kanban/export returns the cached export without the new label for up to 24h. Comment writes (code-2) leave it stale the same way.
findings.suggested_fix: Also call `redis.DeleteFromRedis(board + ":Export")` in createLabel, or switch createLabel to `redis.DeleteAllKeysPrefix(board)`. Make every write that changes board content invalidate the export key.

findings.summary: The getItem and GetLabel cache keys use the client-supplied X-Board header, but the entity lookup ignores the board, so a missing or different header creates entries that invalidation never reaches.
findings.failure_scenario: A client calls GET /kanban/item?id=X without X-Board (Header.Get returns ""). The item is cached under `:item:X`. A later PATCH /kanban/item with `X-Board: B` runs DeleteAllKeysPrefix("B"), which cannot match `:item:X`, so the stale entry keeps being served to any caller that also omits the header. The same happens when one caller reads with board A and another writes with board B for the same item. GetLabel (line 98) has the same issue.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject requests that have no X-Board header, as exportKanban effectively does by indexing `Header["X-Board"][0]`. Better, derive the board from the fetched entity (Item/Label carry boardId) and build the key from that, so reads and invalidation always agree.

findings.summary: Nothing in the run compiled or exercised the change: no `go build ./...`, `go vet`, or local run against Redis.
findings.failure_scenario: The task asked to double-check that the code compiles and to sanity-check caching manually. The only execution was three throwaway /tmp scripts probing encoding/json. The per-edit 'no new diagnostics' notes are the only compile signal. The getKanban regression (code-1) shows exactly what a quick manual GET-twice check would have caught.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` at the repo root. Bring up Redis locally and call each changed GET twice, checking the X-cache header and that hit and miss bodies are identical. Then run a write and confirm the next read misses.

findings.summary: The PR title and body describe a different diff from the one submitted.
findings.failure_scenario: The title is 'Add Redis cache invalidation to kanban create endpoint'. The body says 'This change only covers invalidation on the create path' and that 'adding actual caching (GetFromRedis/SetToRedis...) on the kanban read endpoints ... was not completed'. The diff actually adds read caching to four GET handlers. A reviewer trusting the description would skip the risky part of the change, including the getKanban regression.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the title and body to list every handler that gained caching, with its key scheme, plus the one invalidation added. Call out the known-open gaps: the getKanban hit shape, comment and label invalidation, and the missing build check.

findings.summary: The same eight-line get/check/set block is now copied into four more handlers.
findings.failure_scenario: GetLabel, getItem and exportKanban (and getKanban, in a broken variant) each hand-roll the same cache-hit branch. That is how getKanban ended up with the wrong serialization, and every future fix to hit handling will need six edits.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a small helper, for example `func cachedJSON(c *gin.Context, key string, fetch func() map[string]interface{})`, that does the lookup, sets the HIT header, and populates the cache. Call it from each handler.

findings.summary: The new key suffixes use inconsistent casing (`:Label:`, `:item:`, `:Export`, `:Kanban`) next to the existing `:Labels` and `:items:page:`.
findings.failure_scenario: Mixed singular/plural and capitalization make it easy to write a DeleteFromRedis for the wrong key (for example `:Item:` vs `:item:`) and silently miss invalidation.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one convention (for example lowercase `:label:`, `:item:`, `:export:`, `:kanban`) and add key-builder helpers or constants so reads and invalidations share a single definition.

process_review.summary: The orchestrator started well. One ask survey (trace lines 5-30) produced an accurate, detailed briefing, which was passed to the coder almost verbatim. But it also spawned a pointless 'placeholder' ask at line 3. The coder respected read-before-edit: kanban.go was read at lines 34/36 before the four str_replace calls at 67-80. However, it re-read files the survey had already covered and read whole files where list_symbols or a window would have done. It wrote getKanban caching at line 80 even though line 59 had just shown that GetKanban returns a string. It only realised the serialization mismatch afterwards, through three near-identical /tmp probe scripts (82, 87, 89). The loop_control judge then enforced stop_early at line 90 (repeating_itself 0.65, making_progress 0.13). A write_gate flag on the GetLabel edit (line 69, matches_stated_intent 0.14, surfaced in the line 71 result) was never acted on. The task explicitly asked for a compile check, but no `go build` ever appears in the trace. The run left a known regression and a missing requirement, and the orchestrator did not resume the work; the PR (#18) was opened in that partial state. Spending about $0.90, 41 turns and 45 tool calls on a roughly 40-line, single-file change is disproportionate, and even at that cost the task was not finished.

findings.summary: The coder spent its last turns on repeated /tmp probe scripts until loop_control enforced stop_early, leaving a known bug unfixed and a required invalidation unwritten.
findings.evidence: Line 90 loop_control response: making_progress 0.13, repeating_itself 0.65. stats.json records engine_judge_decisions {tag: loop_control, outcome: stop_early, enforced: true} = 1. The coder's final report: 'work stopped mid-task by orchestrator instruction before completion'; comment-handler invalidation and the getKanban fix are listed as leftovers.

findings.evidence: Lines 82, 87 and 89 each write a /tmp/niltest*.go reimplementing getItemFromRedis. Line 87 already printed `unmarshal err: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go value of type map[string]interface {}` / `false map[]`, which answers the question. Line 89 reruns the same probe with an extra print ('treated as HIT with garbage data'). The exec_approval judges at lines 85 and 88 returned errors, and line 81 scored escapes_workspace 0.89 because the scripts write outside the worktree.

The coder's own report says: 'Did not run go build ./... (or any build/compile command) against the actual repo'. stats.json shows 3 coder run_command calls in total.

findings.evidence: Line 69 write_gate: matches_stated_intent 0.14 (the only write_gate 'flag' decision in stats.json, enforced=false). The str_replace result at line 71 includes '[engine: judge flagged this diff -- may not accomplish what was asked]'. The next action (line 76) is an unrelated getItem edit with reasoning 'Now `getItem`:'. The final report admits: 'I did not re-examine that flag before being cut off'.

findings.evidence: Line 59 showed `func GetKanban(userAccountId string) string`. Line 40 showed GetItemFromRedis unmarshalling into `map[string]interface{}`. The str_replace at line 80 still writes `redis.AddItemToRedis(userAccount+":Kanban", res)` and `c.JSON(http.StatusOK, resCache)` on a hit, with no reasoning recorded. The mismatch was only investigated afterwards (lines 82-89).

findings.evidence: Line 3: ask {"task": "placeholder"} spawned agent 42264636, which reported 'No task was provided'. The orchestrator then said: 'I made an error in my last turn by spawning a second placeholder ask call'. The merge_gate at line 13 scored accomplished_its_brief 0.29.

findings.evidence: write_gate at lines 66, 74 and 78 all returned failed: true with an empty response. merge_gate at line 91 failed. stats.json shows 14 judge requests with result=error, including 3 write_gate and 3 loop_control. The broken getKanban edit (line 80) went through with write_gate at line 78 errored.

findings.summary: After the coder stopped with a known regression, the orchestrator neither resumed it nor produced the requested PR-description paragraph, so a partial, misdescribed PR (#18) was opened.
findings.evidence: The orchestrator's final message lists the getKanban regression, the missing comment invalidation and the missing build check. It then asks the user whether to continue, instead of resuming with continue_from=b4d9ffa3 in this unattended run. The PR body that was published contradicts the actual diff ('This change only covers invalidation on the create path').

strengths: The ask survey was accurate and thorough, and it was handed to the coder with the exact existing cache pattern and route table.
The new caching code follows the existing GetLabels/getItems shape, including the X-cache header and reuse of the shared 24h TTL helper.
Read-before-edit was respected on every edit, and each edit was a single, well-scoped str_replace.
The coder's final report (and the orchestrator's) honestly listed the regression, the missing invalidation and the missing build check rather than claiming success.
concerns: GET /kanban regresses: every cache hit returns `{}` as JSON instead of the board id as text.
The core requirement fails: comment writes never invalidate the cached getItem or export data, and createLabel leaves the export cache stale.
Cache keys depend on an optional client header, so entries can escape invalidation.
The code was never compiled or run, despite the task's explicit request.
The PR title and body misdescribe the diff.
The loop_control stop_early fired after repeated probing, the write_gate flag was ignored, and many judge calls errored, so several edits went unscreened.
About $0.90, 41 turns and 45 tool calls for an unfinished roughly 40-line change.
overall_assessment.narrative: Code and process fail for the same reason. The engine gathered the right context, but the coder did not reason through types before editing. It wired a string-returning function into map-only cache helpers, then spent its remaining budget re-proving that mistake in /tmp scripts until the loop judge cut it off. As a result, the PR ships a user-visible regression on GET /kanban, misses invalidation on the comment and label writes the task explicitly required, and was never compiled. Its description does not match its contents. The caching pattern itself is right, so a focused follow-up could make this mergeable: fix getKanban, add invalidation to the comment and label writes, key on a trusted board id, run go build, and rewrite the PR text.
